card.law_is_about: Stabilising statutory health insurance contributions, including ending reimbursement for homeopathic and anthroposophic services.
card.they_want: Retain insurers’ ability to reimburse those treatments as additional benefits.
card.they_claim: Almost all studies in a cited review found comparable or better outcomes at similar or lower costs.
card.the_problem: The review’s cost categories differ, but similarity depends on significance, population and payer perspective; no error is established.

request_quote.original: den letzten Satz im neuen § 11 Absatz 6 zu streichen
request_quote.translation_en: Translation of request fragment: delete the last sentence in the new section 11(6)

correction: Unresolved: Figure 2 classifies 14 studies as jointly favourable, one neutral and six with higher costs. That classification alone does not disprove the submission’s qualitative description: some differences are nonsignificant, differ between adults and children, or concern societal rather than social-insurer costs. Do not assert 15/21 as a hard bound on similar or lower costs.
effect: No established correction to the policy argument. The lead identifies a source-description question requiring study-level interpretation.
limits: No proven factual error, clinical ineffectiveness, or net GKV cost effect is established. The qualitative terms almost all and similar require careful interpretation of the underlying comparisons.
context_checked: Read the complete homeopathy section on submission pages 5–10, its references, and the review’s methods, results, Figure 2, discussion and conclusion. The submission makes the joint outcome-and-cost assertion before inferring possible GKV relief; its separate arguments about choice, small expenditure and insurer discretion remain independent.
alternative_explanations: Independent adversarial review found: Kass 2020 includes nonsignificant atopic-dermatitis cost differences; Ostermann 2021 has lower costs in children and higher in adults; Trichard 2004 has similar social-security costs despite higher societal/patient costs. These can reconcile some higher-cost classifications with similar costs in the submission’s insurance context.
materiality_explanation: Potentially minor if a numerical overstatement is confirmed; currently unresolved. The submission also relies on several separate policy grounds.
direction_explanation: The asserted consistency supports reimbursement, but an actual error has not been established. Direction is null; the potential argumentative effect remains conditional.

independent_ai.verdict: downgrade to unresolved lead due to cost-comparison context
